title: Victim support referral kit
summary: A collection of nouns and verbs for a victim services program's referral kit: referral options drafted from a public services directory by service type, language, hours and access needs, and a plain referral checklist, while every conversation, safety step, decision and contact stays with trained advocates and nothing accuses anyone.
boundaries: Use only made-up, clearly marked test data.
Steps marked for a person never go to an agent.
Outputs stay surface_only in the requester's scope.
Importing the pack writes nothing and enqueues nothing.

nouns.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for a victim support referral options agent kit

value.lets_workers: Prepare referral options from a public services directory, filtered only by the service needs an advocate enters, with each entry's last verified date, and draft a plain checklist for the referral. The agent never sees a person's story, name, contact details or location. Trained advocates hold every conversation, do all safety planning, and make every referral with the person's consent.
human_only: Do safety planning with the person.
Decide and make the referral with the person's consent.
rules: Use only made-up, clearly marked test data. Never put a real person's details into the kit, a test case or an output.
Steps marked for a person stay with people. The agent drafts or helps; it never decides about a person and never contacts anyone.
Tools are read-only. Anything that changes records outside the requester's scope is a person's step.

provenance_notes.note: The marketplace's example of this kit. It holds only the catalog's own fields and points at this pack's kit and need nouns by value digest, so the kit has one source.

One recorded example run of the kit on a desktop computer with made-up data: check, build and independent review with the marketplace's own pipeline, zero model calls. Not a hosted run or an evaluation.

nouns.title: Victim Support Referral Options Kit
nouns.category_reason: The agent's whole setup as one noun: its step map and pins to every part.

value.summary: Drafts referral options from a public services directory, filtered by service type, language, hours and access needs, and a plain referral checklist for advocates. Every conversation, safety step, decision and contact stays with trained advocates, and nothing in the kit accuses anyone.
value.goal: Help a victim services program prepare referral options from a public services directory and a referral checklist, while trained advocates hold every conversation, do all safety planning, decide every referral with the person's consent and make every contact.
value.target_org: Community victim services program with volunteer advocates

step_map.title: Draft referral options from the public services directory
step_map.guidance: Filter the public directory by the service types, languages, hours and access needs the advocate enters, show each option's last verified date, and mark entries older than 90 days as verify first. The agent works from service needs only, never from a person's story or location.

step_map.title: Draft the referral checklist for the advocate
step_map.guidance: List what to confirm with each service before a referral: eligibility in the service's own words, hours, language access, cost, and what the person agreed to share.

step_map.title: Hold the support conversation
step_map.guidance: A trained advocate talks with the person, listens, and asks what kind of help they want. The agent never talks with the person or reads their story.

step_map.title: Do safety planning with the person
step_map.guidance: Safety planning happens only between the person and a trained advocate. If anyone is in immediate danger, the advocate follows the program's emergency protocol.

step_map.title: Decide and make the referral with the person's consent
step_map.guidance: The person decides which options to pursue. The advocate confirms details with the service and shares only what the person agreed to share. The agent never contacts a service about anyone.

nouns.title: Skill: prepare referral options from service needs only

value.name: referral-options-assistant
value.description: Prepares referral options from a public services directory by service type, language, hours and access needs, with each entry's last verified date.
value.instructions: Work only from the public services directory and the service needs the advocate enters: service types, languages, hours and access needs. Never read or ask for a person's story, name, contact details or location. Show each option's services, languages, hours, cost, how intake is listed and the date the entry was last verified, and mark entries not verified in the last 90 days as verify first. Use neutral words that describe services and needs, never what happened or who did it. Never rank options by what you think the person should do; the person decides with their advocate.
refuses: Reading or asking for a person's story, name, contact details or location
Deciding which service a person should use
Contacting a service or a person
Describing anyone as responsible for harm

nouns.title: Checklist a person runs with the victim support referral kit

items: The agent sees service needs only: no names, stories, contact details or locations.

No text describes what happened to anyone or who is responsible for it.
The output holds no names, phone numbers, email addresses, street addresses or case details.

verbs.title: Draft the referral checklist for the advocate
verbs.summary: Draft a plain checklist per option of what the advocate confirms with the service before a referral, in the service's own words.
verbs.outcome: A referral checklist for the advocate.
steps: For each option, list eligibility in the service's own words, hours, language access, cost and how to reach intake as listed.
End every checklist with: the person decides, and share only what they agreed to share.
Leave out any detail about the person.

acceptance.check: The output validates against template.referral-checklist's schema.

The output holds no names, phone numbers, email addresses, street addresses or case details.
